name: GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc.

profile.description: GlobalFoundries is one of the world's largest pure-play semiconductor foundries, manufacturing chips on specialty and mature nodes (FD-SOI, RF-SOI, silicon photonics, power, embedded memory) for customers in smart mobile devices, automotive, IoT, communications infrastructure and data centers. Headquartered in Malta, New York, with fabs in the US, Germany and Singapore, it is majority-owned by Mubadala and IPO'd in October 2021. Revenue was $6.79B in 2025, and the company initiated a $0.12 quarterly dividend in 2026.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): In August 2018 GF halted 7nm and below development to redirect capital into differentiated technologies (FD-SOI, RF-SOI, silicon photonics, power), a pivot that turned a loss-making leading-edge challenger into a profitable specialty foundry, and it has since agreed to acquire MIPS to add RISC-V processor IP [4][5]. AI Deployment (1/2): Leadership frames 'the AI wave moving from cloud to edge' as its growth basis, and the silicon photonics platform supports 200 Gbps+ server links, but no AI revenue or quantified internal AI savings are disclosed [3][4]. Market Share (1/2): A major pure-play foundry with leading positions in FD-SOI and RF-SOI, but revenue of $6.79B (2025) is still below 2022's $8.11B and no share-gain data was found [2]. Pipeline (1/2): Q3 2026 guidance of $1.885B ±$25M (about 5.5% above Q2) and price increases taking effect in 2027 give near-term visibility, but next-generation platform timelines are not quantified [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D of $518M is 7.6% of 2025 revenue (8.1% TTM), modest for a semiconductor company [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): GF describes itself as a manufacturer of essential semiconductors the world relies on to live, work and connect — clear about its role but not distinctive among foundries [6]. Community Impact (1/2): GF publishes an annual corporate responsibility report, is a Responsible Business Alliance member with a goal to cut greenhouse gas emissions 25% by 2030, and was named to Newsweek's America's Most Responsible Companies 2024 list — general corporate citizenship rather than a distinctive, quantified program [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found; Glassdoor shows 3.6/5 on 2,417 reviews with only 43% holding a positive business outlook [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider buying was found; majority owner Mubadala's control is a long-running overhang.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on all 7 growth metrics. Strengths: D/E of 14.2% (1.0), a current ratio of 2.5, and forward P/E of about 21.1x (0.97) — derived from StockAnalysis's 19.61x at $42.65 (implied forward EPS of about $2.17), applied to the $45.85 price [2][7]. Middling metrics: 5-year revenue CAGR of 7.0% ($4.85B in 2020 to $6.79B in 2025; 0.80, 2x weight) and TTM net margin of 10.3% (0.52) [2]. Drags: TTM ROE of only 6.1% (0.40, 2x weight), TTM revenue growth of just 1.4% ($6.94B vs. $6.84B; 0.71) and FMP's forward PEG of 1.98 (0.51, 2x weight) [2]. Weighted score 6.63/10 → 7. Liquidity floor cleared: 4.64M avg volume × $45.85 ≈ $213M/day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): GF physically manufactures wafers in capital-intensive fabs in the US, Germany and Singapore. AI cannot substitute for semiconductor fabrication, and AI proliferation increases demand for the RF, power-management, connectivity and photonics chips GF makes [2][5]. Management positions edge AI and data center optical interconnect (silicon photonics for 200 Gbps+ links) as growth drivers rather than threats, and no analyst commentary was found flagging AI displacement risk [3][4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): GF does not disclose a quantified AI-related revenue figure, so the tiebreaker point is withheld under the rubric.

infinite_game.summary: GF's defining moment through Sinek's lens is the 2018 decision to walk away from the leading-edge race and rebuild around differentiated technologies — real existential flexibility. But its stated purpose remains a functional description, majority ownership by a sovereign fund shapes priorities, and culture signals are average, leaving it mixed rather than infinite.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Essential semiconductors the world relies on to live, work and connect' states what GF makes rather than an idealistic future it is working toward [6]. It does not visibly drive decisions beyond product focus and has not been tested as a cause across leadership eras (Breen succeeded Caulfield in April 2025) [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The April 2025 CEO succession was orderly — Tim Breen, with the company since 2018 and previously COO, took over while Thomas Caulfield moved to Executive Chairman [3]. Glassdoor's 3.6/5 on 2,417 reviews, 72% CEO approval and only 43% positive outlook, along with recent reviews criticizing technical leadership, indicate adequate rather than exceptional trust [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that frames TSMC, Samsung or UMC as rivals to learn from; the 2018 exit was framed around capital returns and differentiation rather than learning from competitors [4].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): In August 2018 GF abandoned 7nm, 5nm and 3nm development — the core identity of a leading-edge foundry — and redirected engineers and capital into FD-SOI, RF-SOI, silicon photonics and power [4]. This painful pivot, which cost it AMD's leading-edge business, redefined the company and enabled the return to profitability, and it continues with the MIPS RISC-V IP acquisition [4][5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Beyond the 2018 exit, GF raised R&D from $428M (2023) to $496M (2024) even as revenue fell 9% and the company posted a $265M net loss, choosing long-term capability over near-term earnings [2]. Since then, capital allocation has shifted toward shareholder returns (initiating a dividend in July 2026) rather than further bold bets [1].

investment_thesis: GlobalFoundries is a strategically important Western specialty foundry entering a margin and pricing upcycle. Q2 2026 revenue of $1.786B grew 6% YoY and 9% sequentially, with revenue and non-IFRS gross margin (29.9%) above the high end of guidance, and Q3 guidance calls for $1.885B ±$25M, 30.5% gross margin and $0.51 non-IFRS EPS [1]. Price increases implemented in Q2 begin flowing into revenue in 2027, and the balance sheet is clean: D/E of 14.2%, a 2.5 current ratio and about $660M of TTM free cash flow to equity supported a first $0.12 quarterly dividend in July 2026 [1][2]. At about 21x forward earnings, well below its $92.55 52-week high, the stock prices in little of GF's silicon photonics and edge-AI optionality [2][7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that GF remains a low-return, slow-growth manufacturer. TTM revenue grew only 1.4%, 2025 revenue of $6.79B is still 16% below 2022's $8.11B, and TTM ROE of 6.1% is well below the cost of capital for a business that spends 16% of revenue on capex [2]. FMP's forward PEG near 2.0 suggests the valuation already assumes a recovery, and the stock's 1.77 beta and drop from the $92.55 high show high volatility [2]. Majority holder Mubadala can sell down and pressure the shares, mature-node pricing faces competition from heavily subsidized Chinese foundries, and the Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED, LGBT Activism) is a faith-alignment concern for IOWN investors despite 21 positive attributions.
key_catalysts: Delivery of Q3 2026 guidance of $1.885B revenue and 30.5% non-IFRS gross margin, followed by 2027 revenue uplift as Q2 2026 price increases take effect [1]
Silicon photonics design wins for AI data center optical interconnect (200 Gbps+ links) and edge-AI chips, which could lift GF's growth rate above its 7% 5-year revenue CAGR [2][4]
Integration of MIPS RISC-V processor IP into GF's platforms, letting it offer more complete solutions to customers [5]
key_risks: Low returns on a capital-heavy model: TTM ROE of 6.1% and capex at 16% of revenue, with 2025 revenue still 16% below the 2022 peak [2]
Mature-node overcapacity and price competition from state-subsidized Chinese foundries, which could undercut the 2027 price increases [1]
Mubadala majority-ownership overhang and possible secondary sales, on a stock with a 1.77 beta that has fallen from $92.55 to $45.85 [2]
